skills.trigger: When evaluating the distribution of pulmonary opacities on a chest X-ray to differentiate drug-induced pneumonitis (e.g., amiodarone) from other etiologies.
steps: Assess the symmetry of the lung fields to determine if opacities are bilateral or unilateral.
Evaluate the vertical distribution by comparing the density of infiltrates in the upper zones versus the middle and lower zones.
Identify if the pattern is predominantly interstitial or alveolar and concentrated in the mid-to-lower lungs.

skills.trigger: When correlating radiographic patterns with specific drug toxicities to distinguish amiodarone-induced pneumonitis from mimics.
steps: Confirm the presence of bilateral, patchy opacities with a predilection for the middle and lower pulmonary fields.
Exclude diagnoses characterized by strictly upper-lobe predominance or unilateral distribution.
Conclude that the specific combination of bilateral involvement and basilar/mid-zone dominance supports amiodarone toxicity over other differentials.
